summary: Quaffing a blessed gain-ability potion reaches potion.c:peffect_gain_ability through peffects, but js/potion.js throws UnsupportedQuaffError at that effect arm. The C function increments each attribute in order through attrib.c:adjattrib; its cursed, Fixed_abil, and unblessed branches use different output and RNG behavior. Port the complete effect with the required attribute-caller environment.

source.branch: peffect_gain_ability first checks cursed and Fixed_abil. Otherwise it iterates A_MAX attributes, choosing each index sequentially for blessed potions or with rn2(A_MAX) for unblessed ones, and calls adjattrib(i,1,itmp). It breaks on a successful increment only for unblessed potions. The selected blessed Monk case attempts all six attributes in source order.
callers: potion.c:peffects dispatches POT_GAIN_ABILITY from dopotion and dodrink; js/potion.js:peffects currently throws UnsupportedQuaffError(peffect_gain_ability()).
dependencies: attrib.c:adjattrib is already implemented in js/attrib.js. Supply its required message and state operations and use the returned boolean for the unblessed break exactly as C does.
The potion-effect status counters potion_unkn and potion_nothing are distinct C values; preserve their existing JS owner. The cursed and Fixed_abil branches make no adjattrib call.

evidence: Current saved challenges/evaluations/20260927175933-v9.json reports a stop at segment 0 step 35 with 2 of 37 screens remaining after quaffing a blessed gain-ability potion.

Fresh scan at b6e28d15 reports the explicit UnsupportedQuaffError(peffect_gain_ability()) boundary. C has already produced multiple attribute messages while JavaScript refuses before completing the effect.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/potion.c:peffect_gain_ability at 1030-1053 iterates attributes and uses adjattrib return for the unblessed break; potion.c:peffects dispatches POT_GAIN_ABILITY at 1382. js/potion.js:peffects refuses that arm at about 1450.
